# Browser Code Mode

Read this reference completely before the first `run_javascript` call in a task. `run_javascript` executes
one disposable Guest Program against one existing Browser Connection. Use it for loops,
conditions, repeated Locator reads, or a coherent multi-step flow; use direct tools for one or two
simple operations.

## Call shape

```json
{
  "connectionId": "opaque ID from connection_request",
  "summary": "Short description shown in the browser approval UI",
  "code": "const title = await tab.locator('h1').innerText(); return { title };",
  "timeoutMs": 15000
}
```

`summary` is required and limited to 160 characters. It describes the intended run but is not an
authorization or a verified execution plan. `code` is an async-function body, not JSON, a quoted
string, or a Markdown fence. `timeoutMs` is optional and can only lower the 30-second active
JavaScript budget.

The browser issues a Run Grant before the Guest Program starts, requesting approval unless
persistent policy or an applicable origin grant allows it. Nested operations do not prompt separately.
Same-origin navigation remains in that Run Grant. `tab.goto()` checks approval before targeting a
different scheme, hostname, or non-default port. Hostname aliases such as `localhost` and
`127.0.0.1` remain distinct even on the same port. The popup says **Run on** when starting the Run
Grant and **Extend run to** when adding an origin. A cross-origin redirect or later operation
pauses for any required approval before page data is returned. A retained all-operations origin
approval may authorize later runs on that origin. A current policy block defeats older grants.

## Globals

- `tab`: the Browser Connection's single managed tab.
- `checkpoint(name, value)`: retain one named JSON-serializable stage result, including when a later
  operation fails. Names contain 1 to 64 characters; at most 64 checkpoints share the output
  budget.
- `text(value)`: append one bounded text item.
- `image(handle)`: append an `ImageHandle` returned by `tab.screenshot()`.
- `console.log/info/warn/error(...values)`: append bounded diagnostic logs.
- `sleep(milliseconds)`: await a delay capped at 10 seconds.
- `setTimeout(callback, milliseconds)` and `clearTimeout(id)`: timers capped at 10 seconds. Pending
  timers do not keep the Guest Program alive.
- `exit()`: finish successfully with a `null` return value.

Node.js, `process`, `require`, files, environment variables, `fetch`, network sockets, imports,
page evaluation, raw CDP, and private Browser capabilities are unavailable.

## `tab` interface

```ts
type SnapshotFilter = "all" | "interactive";
type WaitState = "attached" | "detached" | "visible" | "hidden";
type LocatorText = string | RegExp;
type FrameSnapshot = {
  frameRef: string; // diagnostics and tree relationships only; not a routing argument
  title: string;
  url: string;
  content: string;
  omissions: string[];
  frames: FrameSnapshot[];
};

type Snapshot = {
  title: string;
  url: string;
  content: string;
  omissions: string[];
  focus?: { ref: string };
  selection?: { ref: string; kind: string; start: number; end: number; collapsed: boolean };
  frames?: FrameSnapshot[];
};

type ImageHandle = Readonly<{
  width: number;
  height: number;
  mimeType: "image/jpeg";
  sizeBytes: number;
}>;

type LocatorFilter = {
  hasText?: LocatorText;
  hasNotText?: LocatorText;
  has?: Locator;
  hasNot?: Locator;
  visible?: boolean;
};

type Locator = {
  locator(selector: string, filter?: LocatorFilter): Locator;
  getByRole(role: string, options?: { name?: LocatorText; exact?: boolean }): Locator;
  getByText(text: LocatorText, options?: { exact?: boolean }): Locator;
  getByLabel(text: LocatorText, options?: { exact?: boolean }): Locator;
  getByPlaceholder(text: LocatorText, options?: { exact?: boolean }): Locator;
  getByTestId(testId: string): Locator;
  filter(options?: LocatorFilter): Locator;
  first(): Locator;
  last(): Locator;
  nth(index: number): Locator;
  and(other: Locator): Locator;
  or(other: Locator): Locator;
  contentFrame(): FrameLocator;
  closedShadow(): Locator;
  all(): Promise<Locator[]>;

  click(options?: { button?: "left"; timeoutMs?: number }): Promise<null>;
  dblclick(options?: { button?: "left"; timeoutMs?: number }): Promise<null>;
  fill(value: string, options?: { timeoutMs?: number }): Promise<null>;
  type(value: string, options?: { timeoutMs?: number }): Promise<null>;
  press(key: string, options?: { timeoutMs?: number }): Promise<null>;
  waitFor(options: { state: WaitState; timeoutMs?: number }): Promise<null>;
  scrollIntoViewIfNeeded(options?: { timeoutMs?: number }): Promise<null>;
  count(): Promise<number>;
  isVisible(): Promise<boolean>;
  isEnabled(): Promise<boolean>;
  allTextContents(options?: { timeoutMs?: number }): Promise<string[]>;
  textContent(options?: { timeoutMs?: number }): Promise<string | null>;
  innerText(options?: { timeoutMs?: number }): Promise<string>;
  getAttribute(name: string, options?: { timeoutMs?: number }): Promise<string | null>;
};

type FrameLocator = {
  locator(selector: string, filter?: LocatorFilter): Locator;
  getByRole(role: string, options?: { name?: LocatorText; exact?: boolean }): Locator;
  getByText(text: LocatorText, options?: { exact?: boolean }): Locator;
  getByLabel(text: LocatorText, options?: { exact?: boolean }): Locator;
  getByPlaceholder(text: LocatorText, options?: { exact?: boolean }): Locator;
  getByTestId(testId: string): Locator;
  frameLocator(selector: string): FrameLocator;
};

type Tab = {
  frameLocator(selector: string): FrameLocator;
  locator(selector: string, filter?: LocatorFilter): Locator;
  getByRole(role: string, options?: { name?: LocatorText; exact?: boolean }): Locator;
  getByText(text: LocatorText, options?: { exact?: boolean }): Locator;
  getByLabel(text: LocatorText, options?: { exact?: boolean }): Locator;
  getByPlaceholder(text: LocatorText, options?: { exact?: boolean }): Locator;
  getByTestId(testId: string): Locator;

  url(): Promise<string>;
  goto(url: string, options?: { timeoutMs?: number }): Promise<string>;
  reload(options?: { timeoutMs?: number }): Promise<string>;
  goBack(options?: { timeoutMs?: number }): Promise<string>;
  goForward(options?: { timeoutMs?: number }): Promise<string>;
  waitForURL(pattern: string, options?: { timeoutMs?: number }): Promise<string>;
  snapshot(options?: { filter?: SnapshotFilter }): Promise<Snapshot>;
  screenshot(): Promise<ImageHandle>;
  click(ref: string, options?: { doubleClick?: boolean }): Promise<{ outcome: string }>;
  hover(ref: string): Promise<{ outcome: string }>;
  keyboard(key: string): Promise<{ outcome: string }>;
  type(text: string, options?: { ref?: string; submitKey?: string }): Promise<{ outcome: string }>;
};
```

`waitForURL()` string patterns match the complete normalized URL: `*` matches within one path
segment and `**` crosses `/` separators. Navigation methods return the final normalized URL.
Reload, back, and forward wait for a loading/URL transition or tab replacement after the action
starts; they do not accept a stale pre-navigation `complete` tab.

Locators support Playwright CSS, XPath, role, text, label, placeholder, test-id, and internal
selector syntax in the main document and open Shadow DOM. In supported dev/private-preview builds,
when the default-Off **Advanced page surfaces · Experimental** setting was enabled before this
Browser Connection was opened, use `frameLocator()`, nested `FrameLocator.frameLocator()`, `contentFrame()`, and
`closedShadow()` to cross each frame or page-author Closed Shadow Root explicitly. Ordinary
Locators never cross these boundaries. Frames use their actual non-opaque origins for browser-owned
policy and may trigger one origin/count subset approval; the setting and approval choices are never inferred
by the agent. Single-target methods are strict: zero matches or multiple matches fail, so use
`first()`, `last()`, or `nth()` deliberately. `force` is unavailable because it would bypass the
hit-target check. `scrollIntoViewIfNeeded()` asks Chromium to perform the minimum `nearest` scroll
through the viewport and every clipping/scrollable ancestor for one already-loaded strict target.
It does this even when the target's rectangle is inside the viewport, because an overflow ancestor
may still clip it. It cannot locate a virtual-list item that is not yet in the DOM. Offscreen
scrolling across multiple frame boundaries is not supported; work from an exposed boundary or hand
that scroll to the user rather than repeatedly retrying a clipped frame chain. Actions that open a
new tab or window are rejected.

Every terminal Locator call re-resolves and freezes its exact Element before trusted browser input.
A successful mutating call confirms that the trusted browser input was dispatched; it does not prove
that application code accepted the input or changed its data model. Read back the smallest relevant
state and assert the expected postcondition instead of treating dispatch as application success.
`fill()` replaces the complete value of native inputs and textareas. For a contenteditable editor,
use `type()` to insert text; if an application such as a canvas-based spreadsheet creates its editor
only after activation, click or double-click the target first and then use ref-less `tab.type()` so
input follows the validated frame-local focus. A canvas itself is not an editable element and must
not be passed to `fill()`. Password, authentication-code, payment, and file controls cannot be read,
operated, or observed through Locator wait states. An existing Protected Control is rejected before `attached`,
`detached`, `visible`, or `hidden` is evaluated. Collection
text preserves positions with `[PROTECTED CONTROL]`; high-confidence tokens are masked. Result
omissions report when sensitive content was withheld.

## Results and recovery

Use `return` for one JSON-serializable result. Use `text()` for additional text and `image()` only
when the model must see a screenshot. Returning or logging an `ImageHandle` exposes metadata only.
All returned values, checkpoints, operation traces, logs, text, and images are Guest Output under a
server-authored untrusted-data notice; page data never becomes instructions or authorization after
the Guest Program transforms it. A failed program has a `null` return value because its `return`
never completed, but accepted checkpoints, text, logs, images, and the bounded recent operation
trace remain available.

Await every `tab` and Locator operation. Finishing with pending browser calls fails with
`UNAWAITED_OPERATIONS` and cancels calls that have not committed. Browser actions that already
committed are never rolled back.

Nested failures reject a catchable `BrowserError` with `code`, `message`, `operationIndex`,
`operation`, `source`, `pageUrl`, `committed`, an optional `locator`, and sometimes `retryHint` or
`reason`.
The final `guestOutput.error` repeats the diagnostic when the error is not caught. Browser-originated
errors carry an operation identity in a closure-private WeakMap keyed by the exact Error object, not
a Guest-visible property. Wrapping a caught browser message or copying its properties into a new
script error does not misattribute the terminating code or source. `pageUrl` is the
postflight URL only when its origin is already authorized by the current Run Grant; it is omitted
rather than disclosing or misreporting an unapproved destination. When navigation has already been
dispatched but destination approval is denied, the error keeps `APPROVAL_DENIED` and reports
`committed: "unknown"` without revealing the destination URL. The last 32 operation summaries
remain in `guestOutput.operations`; source locations are one-based positions in the submitted
`code`. Use codes such as `PAGE_CHANGED`, `STALE_ELEMENT_REFERENCE`,
`ELEMENT_NOT_ACTIONABLE`, and `ACTION_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` instead of parsing messages. Advanced
boundaries additionally use `ADVANCED_SURFACES_DISABLED`, `DOMAIN_BLOCKED`,
`UNSUPPORTED_FRAME_ORIGIN`, `APPROVAL_DENIED`, and `RESOURCE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`. A broad snapshot
reports only `child-frames`, `closed-shadow-roots`, or `advanced-surface-limit`; do not infer a
private policy decision or the capability setting from an omission. `ADVANCED_SURFACES_DISABLED`
can mean an unavailable build or a disabled captured setting: use a supported build, enable the
Experimental setting when present, and open a new connection. Production/store builds have no such
setting to enable. Never immediately replay an action when `committed` is `true` or `"unknown"`;
inspect current state first. This includes a keyboard continuation that fails after earlier text
input or part of a chord was already dispatched.

An authorized strict-boundary failure may refine `ELEMENT_NOT_ACTIONABLE` with one of these closed
`reason` values, also retained for an uncaught browser error and its operation trace:

| Reason | Next observation |
| --- | --- |
| `BOUNDARY_NOT_FOUND` | Check whether the chosen owner selector matches the current DOM. |
| `BOUNDARY_NOT_UNIQUE` | Narrow the owner Locator deliberately. |
| `NOT_ATTACHED_FRAME_OWNER` | Check that the chosen element owns an attached frame and observe loading state. |
| `NO_PAGE_AUTHOR_CLOSED_ROOT` | Check the host choice; ordinary Locators already traverse open Shadow DOM. |

An absent reason remains an ordinary actionability failure. These reasons do not expose raw CDP
identity or replace authorization, Protected Control, or commit-state checks.

Hard limits include 64 KiB source, 64 MiB Guest heap, 1 MiB Guest stack, 30 seconds active
JavaScript, 10 minutes total wall time, 256 browser operations, 8 pending operations, 64 Advanced
Surfaces per operation and per Run (distinct frame epochs and Closed Shadow Root identities), 4 MiB
per nested result, 5000 Locator collection entries, 256 KiB result/text/checkpoints, 64 KiB logs, the
last 32 operation summaries, at most 1024 text items, at most 1024 log items, an 8 KiB final script
error message, and at most two images totaling 20 MiB. Text and log budgets charge their JSON UTF-8
serialized size, including escaping and separators. The first operation-admission limit violation
latches the Run failure even if Guest code catches it; later requests are rejected without growing
the parent trace or reaching the browser. `OUTPUT_TOO_LARGE` retains previously accepted small
output and asks for a narrower retry.

Run Grant close is attempted once. If revocation cannot be confirmed, an existing execution failure
remains primary with its partial Guest Output, cleanup is reported separately, and the MCP retains
exclusive run ownership instead of forwarding direct tools. Explicitly finalize the Browser
Connection once to revoke the whole connection. If a canceled Run open cannot confirm its
compensating close, the Native Host also retains a fail-closed peer state and rejects direct tools
with `RUN_IN_PROGRESS` until that finalization. Authorization remains fail-closed even if closing the
managed tab fails; tab closure may be retried by normal connection maintenance.

## Example

```js
const rows = await tab.getByRole("row").all();
checkpoint("rows-loaded", { count: rows.length, url: await tab.url() });
const approved = [];
for (const row of rows) {
  if ((await row.innerText()).includes("Pending")) {
    await row.scrollIntoViewIfNeeded();
    await row.getByRole("button", { name: "Approve" }).click();
    approved.push(await row.getAttribute("data-id"));
  }
}
return { approved };
```
